title: British Food: God Save the Cuisine
description: A celebration of the United Kingdom's proudest culinary achievements — from chip butties to spotted dick.

questions.prompt: The cooked breakfast featuring eggs, bacon, sausage, beans, and black pudding:
questions.explanation: The Full English is also known as a 'fry-up' — because everything, somehow, ends up in the frying pan.

questions.prompt: A 'chip butty' is a British sandwich filled with:
questions.explanation: A chip butty is exactly what it sounds like: chips (fries) crammed into soft white bread, with optional ketchup.

questions.prompt: The British pudding with a name that has made foreign menus awkward since 1850:
questions.explanation: Spotted Dick is a steamed suet pudding with raisins — 'spotted' refers to the fruit and 'dick' likely derives from 'dough.'

questions.prompt: Marmite, the British spread applied to toast that divides families, is made from:
questions.explanation: Marmite is yeast extract and is famously polarising — its slogan 'Love it or hate it' is the most honest food advertising in history.

questions.prompt: The dark, murky condiment called brown sauce slathered on bacon sandwiches contains:
questions.explanation: Brown sauce like HP Sauce blends tamarind, tomatoes, and spices — best described as 'ketchup that gave up.'

questions.prompt: The British 'meal' of canned baked beans poured over sliced white toast:
questions.explanation: Beans on toast has been a perfectly acceptable British dinner since the 1920s, no shame required.

questions.prompt: The lurid green side dish served alongside fish and chips at British chippies:
questions.explanation: Mushy peas are dried marrowfat peas soaked and boiled into a vibrant green mush — the colour of ambition, the texture of regret.

questions.prompt: Haggis, Scotland's beloved national dish, is traditionally cooked inside:
questions.explanation: Haggis is oatmeal, onions, and sheep offal stuffed into a sheep's stomach and boiled — Scotland is very proud of this.

questions.prompt: Coronation chicken, created in 1953 for Queen Elizabeth II, is cold chicken in:
questions.explanation: Coronation chicken blends cold chicken with curried mayo and dried fruit — a royal invention that became a supermarket sandwich filling.

questions.prompt: The British instant snack that once used 'the slag of all snacks' as its actual slogan:
questions.explanation: Pot Noodle is a just-add-boiling-water instant noodle pot that embraced its trashy reputation in its own advertising.

questions.prompt: The beloved British chocolate bar with a distinctive wafer texture, known for its slogan 'a finger of Fudge':
questions.explanation: Cadbury Fudge is a chocolate-covered wafer bar with a catchy jingle — the 'finger of Fudge' slogan is iconic British advertising.
